raw_case_text:
This was a second case of a 43-year-old male laborer, diagnosed as HIV positive 2 years back who was on ART and anti-tubercular treatment for the past 9 months. He presented with a 7 month history of asymptomatic skin lesions all over his body. Physical examination revealed multiple bilateral asymmetrical diffuse, papulonodular, non-itchy skin lesions of size 2-25 mm on the face, trunk and extremities. Lesions first appeared on the arm and progressively spread to involve the face, legs and trunk [Figure 3]. There were no signs of ulceration and scarring. There was no lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly. There was no history of travel to endemic areas of leishmaniasis. The patient was initially suspected to be suffering from histoplasmosis, but skin biopsy taken from the nodules ruled it out. Laboratory investigations revealed anemia (Hb-9.1 g/dL). Liver function tests, renal function tests and lipid profile were normal. Ultrasonography of the abdomen was normal. His CD4 count was 50 cells/muL and HIV viral load was 1750 copies/mL. Punch biopsy of skin lesions revealed sheets of histiocytic cells in the sub epithelial tissue, stuffed with numerous amastigotes of Leishmania. Mild lymphocytic and plasma cell infiltrate was also noted [Figure 4].
The patient was treated with ketoconazole 200 mg twice daily and 450 mg rifampicin daily for 1 month along with ART (nevirapine, stavudine and lamivudine). The patient initially responded to treatment but later on expired due to chest infection.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 43-year-old HIV-positive male laborer presented with a 7-month history of widespread asymptomatic papulonodular skin lesions over his face, trunk, and extremities.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Seven months before presentation, the patient developed painless, non-pruritic papulonodular skin lesions on his arm that progressively spread to involve his face, trunk, and lower extremities.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with HIV infection 2 years prior; treated with antiretroviral therapy (nevirapine, stavudine, lamivudine) and antitubercular therapy for the preceding 9 months; laborer with no history of travel to known leishmaniasis-endemic regions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Taking ART (nevirapine, stavudine, lamivudine) and antitubercular medications; negative for pruritus or ulceration.

objective.physical_examination: Multiple bilateral, asymmetrical, diffuse, non-ulcerated, non-scarring papulonodular skin lesions measuring 2-25 mm distributed over the face, trunk, and upper and lower extremities; no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed anemia (Hb 9.1 g/dL) with normal liver function tests, renal function tests, and lipid profile. Abdominal ultrasonography was normal.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 50 cells/uL and HIV viral load was 1,750 copies/mL. Skin punch biopsy demonstrated sheets of subepithelial histiocytes packed with numerous Leishmania amastigotes and a mild lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Disseminated cutaneous histoplasmosis was excluded by skin punch biopsy histopathology demonstrating abundant intracellular Leishmania amastigotes within dermal histiocytes, confirming atypical diffuse Cutaneous Leishmaniasis in an HIV-infected patient. Treatment with oral ketoconazole (200 mg twice daily) and oral rifampicin (450 mg daily) for 1 month alongside ART produced an initial clinical response, but the patient subsequently died of a chest infection.
